input.explanation:
Fault: `average_spend_per_item_this_month` divided `total_this_month_cents` by `len(bought)` with no check that the account actually made any purchases in the current month. Any account page for a shopper with zero purchases this month (very common - new accounts, dormant accounts, and everyone at the start of a month) hit `x // 0` and raised ZeroDivisionError at spend_summary.py:32. The `monthly-spend-feature` flag flip at 13:55 merely routed real traffic down this path, so the error rate jumped to 21-34%; the flag was not the fault, this unguarded division was.

Fix: the function now returns 0 when there are no in-month purchases (an average over nothing is zero spend per item, which is what the account page wants to render), and it is defensive about a missing/None monthly total. This makes the code safe with the flag on, so `monthly-spend-feature` can be turned back on permanently.

Also completed `Account.__init__`, which only stored `purchases` and silently dropped `total_cents` / `total_this_month_cents`, leaving the attribute the summary reads undefined.

Tests: added the failing case (shopper with no purchases this month returns 0 instead of raising) alongside the normal case, the mixed in-month/out-of-month case, and the missing-total case.

files.content:
def average_spend_per_item_this_month(account):
    """Average spend, in cents, per item bought in the current month.

    Accounts with no purchases in the current month are a normal case (new
    accounts, dormant accounts, and every account at the start of a month),
    so the average over an empty basket is reported as 0 rather than being
    allowed to raise ZeroDivisionError into the account page.
    """
    bought = [p for p in account.purchases or [] if p.in_current_month]
    if not bought:
        return 0
    total = getattr(account, "total_this_month_cents", 0) or 0
    return total // len(bought)

from io_shop.accounts import Account
from io_shop.spend_summary import average_spend_per_item_this_month


class Purchase:
    def __init__(self, in_current_month):
        self.in_current_month = in_current_month


def test_the_monthly_average_is_correct_for_a_shopper_who_did_buy():
    account = Account(
        purchases=[Purchase(True), Purchase(True)],
        total_cents=5000,
        total_this_month_cents=1000,
    )

    assert average_spend_per_item_this_month(account) == 500


def test_the_monthly_average_is_zero_for_a_shopper_who_bought_nothing_this_month():
    # This is the case that raised ZeroDivisionError when the
    # monthly-spend-feature flag was turned on.
    account = Account(
        purchases=[Purchase(False), Purchase(False)],
        total_cents=5000,
        total_this_month_cents=0,
    )

    assert average_spend_per_item_this_month(account) == 0


def test_the_monthly_average_is_zero_for_an_account_with_no_purchases_at_all():
    account = Account(purchases=[], total_cents=0, total_this_month_cents=0)

    assert average_spend_per_item_this_month(account) == 0


def test_only_current_month_purchases_count_towards_the_average():
    account = Account(
        purchases=[Purchase(True), Purchase(False), Purchase(True)],
        total_cents=9000,
        total_this_month_cents=900,
    )

    assert average_spend_per_item_this_month(account) == 450


def test_a_missing_monthly_total_is_treated_as_zero_spend():
    account = Account(
        purchases=[Purchase(True)],
        total_cents=100,
        total_this_month_cents=None,
    )

    assert average_spend_per_item_this_month(account) == 0

input.summary: Guard monthly average spend against accounts with no purchases this month (ZeroDivisionError)
